name: DenverSEO.io SEO and AI Search Glossary

terms.definition: Structuring content so AI assistants and search features can lift it as a direct answer. Rewards clear definitions, specific facts and structured data.
A bot operated by an AI company that fetches web pages, either to train models (like GPTBot) or to answer live questions and cite sources (like OAI-SearchBot).
An AI-generated summary Google shows at the top of some search results, with links to the sources it drew from.
Software that takes actions for a user, such as researching vendors, filling forms or booking appointments, instead of only answering questions.
A text description of an image in the alt attribute. Used by screen readers and by search engines to understand images.
The clickable words of a link. It tells people and search engines what the linked page is about.
A search tool that responds with a written answer instead of a list of links, such as ChatGPT search, Perplexity or Google AI Mode.
A link from another website to yours. Links from relevant, trusted sites are a strong signal of authority.
Microsoft's web crawler for Bing. Bing's index also feeds several AI tools, including Microsoft Copilot.
A navigation trail showing where a page sits in a site's hierarchy. BreadcrumbList schema describes it to search engines.
The preferred version of a page when several URLs show the same content, declared with a rel=canonical link.
A link or source reference an AI answer shows for information it used. Being cited is the AI-era version of ranking.
Anthropic's web crawler. Anthropic also documents separate agents for search and user-initiated fetching.
A Core Web Vitals metric for unexpected layout movement. Good is 0.1 or less.
Google's set of real-user metrics for loading (LCP), responsiveness (INP) and visual stability (CLS).
How many URLs a search engine is able and willing to crawl on a site in a given time. Matters mostly for very large sites.
The process of bots fetching web pages and following links to discover more pages.
The qualities Google's quality rater guidelines use to evaluate content. Trust is the most important of the four.
A distinct, identifiable thing, such as a business, person, place or product, that search engines and AI models recognize and connect to facts.
A highlighted excerpt Google sometimes shows at the top of results to answer a query directly.
The practice of earning visibility and citations inside AI-generated answers from tools like ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity.
Google's free listing for local businesses that appears in Maps and the local pack.
A robots.txt control token that lets sites choose whether Google may use their content for Gemini and related AI training and grounding. It does not affect Google Search.
Google's main web crawler for Search.
OpenAI's crawler for collecting training data. Separate from OAI-SearchBot, which supports ChatGPT search.
A browser without a visible window, used by search engines and testing tools to render pages and run JavaScript.
An attribute that tells search engines which language or regional version of a page to show.
The database of pages a search engine has stored and can show in results.
A Core Web Vitals metric for how quickly a page responds to user input. Good is 200 milliseconds or less.
A link from one page to another on the same site. It helps discovery and signals which pages matter.
The script-based format Google recommends for structured data, written as JSON inside a script tag.
Google's database of entities and the facts connecting them, which powers knowledge panels and informs AI features.
A Core Web Vitals metric for when the main content finishes loading. Good is 2.5 seconds or less.
An AI model trained on large amounts of text that can generate and understand language, such as the models behind ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.
A proposed Markdown file at a site's root that summarizes the site for language models and links to key pages.
The block of three map listings Google shows for local searches.
A short summary of a page in its HTML head. Search engines may show it as the snippet under the title.
A robots meta tag or header telling search engines not to include a page in their index.
OpenAI's crawler for surfacing websites in ChatGPT search results.
A page with no internal links pointing to it.
Perplexity's crawler for building the index that powers its cited answers.
Creating many search-targeted pages from a template and a structured dataset.
The question or instruction a user gives an AI model. Prompts are the new search queries.
A technique where an AI search system breaks one question into many related searches, then combines the results into one answer.
A method where an AI system retrieves relevant documents first, then generates an answer grounded in them. Most AI search works this way.
A permanent redirect sending visitors and search engines from an old URL to a new one, passing along its signals.
Running a page's code, especially JavaScript, to produce the final content a user sees.
A search result with extra visual features, such as stars, FAQs, prices or images, often powered by structured data.
A text file at a site's root that tells crawlers which paths they may access. Defined in RFC 9309.
The shared vocabulary of types and properties used to write structured data, maintained by the major search engines.
What the searcher actually wants: information, a specific site, a comparison or a purchase.
The page of results a search engine shows for a query.
Generating a page's HTML on the server so it arrives complete, rather than building it in the browser.
A file listing the URLs a site wants search engines to know about, often with last-modified dates.
A schema property marking sections of a page that are suited to text-to-speech, such as for voice assistants.
A site served as pre-built HTML files. Fast, secure and easy for any crawler to read.
Code, usually JSON-LD, that describes a page's content in a standard format so machines can understand it precisely.
The work of making a site crawlable, renderable, indexable, fast and well structured for search engines.
The HTML title of a page, usually shown as the clickable headline in search results.
A search where the user gets an answer on the results page or in an AI response and does not click through to a website.
